info.title: Interview Monitoring API
info.description:
REST API for the interview-monitoring platform: a candidate's phone streams its camera through
LiveKit, and the interviewer's dashboard watches and analyzes it live.

### Conventions
* Bodies are **JSON** (`Content-Type: application/json`, max 64 KB). JSON fields are **camelCase**.
* Errors always look like `{"error": {"code", "message", "details?"}}`.
* Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`2030-01-02T10:00:00.000Z`).

### Authentication
* **Interviewer / admin** — `POST /api/auth/login` (or `register`) returns a `token` and sets the httpOnly
  `im_session` cookie. Send either `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or the cookie. Sessions last 8 hours.
* **Candidate** — `POST /api/interviews/{id}/join` returns a token scoped to **one** interview (4 hours),
  sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

### Common status codes
`400` invalid input · `401` not signed in · `403` no access · `404` no match (also a wrong candidate name) ·
`410` interview ended · `413`/`415` bad body · `429` rate limited · `503` LiveKit/database unreachable.

post.description: Creates an `INTERVIEWER` (or `ADMIN` when `adminCode` matches the server's code), signs the user in and sets the `im_session` cookie. Limited to 10 per hour per IP.
Returns a session token and sets the `im_session` cookie. A wrong password and an unknown email return the same error. Limited to 30 per 10 minutes per IP and 10 per 10 minutes per email.

post.description: The candidate proves access with the interview ID and their name and must accept the monitoring notice (`consentAccepted: true`). Name matching ignores case and extra spaces; the ID tolerates lower case, spaces and look-alike letters. A wrong name gets the **same** 404 as a wrong ID, so IDs can't be discovered. Returns a candidate token scoped to this interview. Limited to 20 per 10 minutes per IP.

Tells the room, then deletes it so media stops immediately. Candidate tokens stop working because the status is checked on every request. Status becomes `COMPLETED` if it had started, otherwise `CANCELLED`. Calling it twice is harmless.

post.description: Issues a short-lived token for the interview's room (creating the room if needed). **A candidate's first request here starts the interview** (`SCHEDULED` → `ACTIVE`). Candidates always get the same identity (`candidate-<id>`), so a second device replaces the first. Candidates may publish camera and microphone only; interviewers are subscribe-only; nobody may publish data. Limited to 30 per minute per user.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid/expired (`unauthorized`).

post.description: LiveKit's own view of the session, independent of what any client reports. Not for the frontend. The request must be signed by LiveKit (the `Authorization` header carries a JWT covering the raw body). Redelivered webhooks don't create duplicate events.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid/expired (`unauthorized`).

post.description:
Clients pick an `eventType` from an allowlist; the wording and severity come from the server's catalog, so clients can't author event text.

- Candidate may report: `camera_permission_error`, `calibration_passed`, `candidate_reconnecting`, `candidate_reconnected`, `network_unstable`, `network_recovered`, `app_backgrounded`, `app_foregrounded`.
- Interviewer may report: `video_stopped`, `video_resumed`, `network_unstable`, `network_recovered`.

Limited to 60 per minute per interview and side.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid/expired (`unauthorized`).

post.description: Phones report `calibration`; once streaming starts, the interviewer's dashboard analyzes the received video and reports `stream_analysis`. Each side is held to its own `source` (403 otherwise). Stream-analysis changes can add timeline events (`screen_detected`, `screen_lost`, `visibility_dropped`, `positioning_corrected`), returned in `events`. Limited to 120 per minute per interview and side.

401.description: Not signed in, or the token is invalid/expired (`unauthorized`).

post.summary: Analyse a screenshot of the candidate's screen
post.description: The interviewer's dashboard sends a screenshot (base64, up to 8 MB). A vision model identifies the visible application and returns exactly six fields. When a new application needing review appears, a `screen_app_review` (HIGH) or `screen_app_changed` (MEDIUM) event is added to the timeline; the same application staying visible does not repeat it. A HIGH alert means review is recommended, not misuse. AI failures return an error (never a made-up analysis). Limited to 30 per minute per interview.
